rationale: ⚠️ The connection configuration needs a desired status enum; the referenced object instead describes a detailed status report. String serialization is consistent with the model, making the schema reference the likely error.

⚠️ The explicitly supported widget description has no destination in either domain or persistence fields. Mapping the submitted widget therefore discards meaningful input; incomplete implementation support is more likely than an intentionally unusable contract field.

⚠️ Both the contract and Parameter annotation identify a required query value. The method omits the actual QueryParam binding annotation, leaving an entity parameter despite its documented query intent.
⚠️ Slug filtering is explicitly documented and guarded by the supplied slug, but the equality condition uses name. This is a wrong-variable implementation error.

⚠️ The environment is passed into category lookup, but only the key fallback uses it. A successful global ID lookup returns immediately without checking environment membership, defeating the operation scope.

⚠️ The registered route supplies projectName, while the GET method requires projectId without an explicit binding name. The handler cannot bind the advertised project variable; implementation binding is inconsistent with its route.
⚠️ The DELETE route inherits projectName but the method requires projectId. Its required path binding has no matching template variable, indicating an implementation binding defect.
⚠️ The user route, deleteUsers method, user repository, and self-deletion safeguard consistently concern users. The annotation describing launches is an isolated documentation mistake.

⚠️ MQTT 5 is an explicit connection type supported by the model, and retrieval serializes that stored type normally. The contract enumeration is incomplete rather than the implementation inventing an unsupported value.
⚠️ The plural token operation, declared List return type, and DAO list query agree on collection cardinality. The response annotation lacks the list container and is the likely specification defect.

⚠️ Invalid UUID validation deliberately produces BadRequest, which the shared mapper correctly turns into 400. Documenting that foreseeable input-validation response is more plausible than changing the implementation to suppress it.

⚠️ Export is exposed beneath a project and checks path-project access, yet the controller passes no project membership to the handler. The handler retrieves launchId globally, leaving the launch-to-project relationship unchecked.
⚠️ The model explicitly supports mqtt-5 and the collection response serializes each connection using its model serializer. The schema enumeration omits a supported type and is likely stale.
⚠️ The router registration, handler name, and handler documentation consistently use plural manifests. The singular contract path is the isolated inconsistency and most likely a specification typo.
⚠️ The logged-in-user endpoint returns the stored User, whose JSON getter exposes the explicit TOS_VERSION_2 enum member. The contract enum has not represented the full supported version set.

⚠️ Deletion receives an environment execution context but fetches and deletes by global category ID without verifying its environment. Using context for audit does not enforce the advertised resource scope.

⚠️ The address schema names townName, while the domain uses city. The request mapper declares only automatic mapping with no rename instruction, so translating this supported field is missing from the implementation.

⚠️ For the stated cardinality mismatch, the method and DAO return a token list, fitting the plural operation. The single-Token annotation omits its collection container; the separate DAO-provider choice does not justify scalar cardinality.

⚠️ MergeThing has an explicit authorization branch checking unrestricted WRITE for every affected leaf. This deliberate granular policy supports partial updates; the blanket root-WRITE requirement appears overly restrictive documentation.
⚠️ Metadata is explicitly defined as a JSON object field and serialized through metadata.toJson. The contract string type conflicts with that structured model and is the likely schema error.

⚠️ The model already parses and preserves allowedImportAdditions, but the PUT route reconstructs entries using overloads that default additions to an empty set. The route drops supported input rather than honoring the contract.

⚠️ A connection configuration stores its desired ConnectivityStatus and serializes its enum name. The referenced ConnectionStatus object describes a richer status report, indicating an incorrect schema reference for the configuration property.

⚠️ User retrieval returns the persisted model directly, including its JSON-exposed TOSVersion enum. TOS_VERSION_2 is explicitly supported in that model, making the narrower contract enumeration incomplete.

⚠️ The slug parameter is documented as a project filter and controls entry to the condition, but name supplies the slug comparison value. This wrong-variable expression violates the intended filtering behavior.

⚠️ Updating accepts widget descriptions in the contract, but both mapped models omit that field. The update pipeline cannot retain the submitted description, suggesting incomplete implementation of an explicit input feature.

⚠️ The contract promises the created instance ID. The handler discards the creation result and returns a responder without attaching a payload, suggesting omitted response construction rather than an unnecessary schema.
⚠️ Policy-deletion errors use the shared responder and serializer, which deliberately wraps errors in an object. The contract models only the inner array and omits the common response envelope.

⚠️ The controller explicitly permits omitted attributes and forwards them unchanged. The content-loading branch passes that nullable array directly to Lists.newArrayList, so the implementation fails to handle a permitted omission.

⚠️ The response schema uses townName but the domain address exposes city. The automatic response mapper supplies no explicit rename, leaving the supported address field without the required translation.

⚠️ The trailing-slash alias binds projectName while the same method requires projectKey. The implementation must align its registered alias and required binding to serve the advertised preference request.

⚠️ Instance-deletion errors pass through the shared responder into an object containing errors. The centralized serializer establishes an intentional envelope that the contract incorrectly replaces with a top-level array.
⚠️ The path and description concern the entire features collection, with feature IDs supplied in the body. Requiring featureId as a path parameter absent from the template is a specification error.

⚠️ Bulk update receives project membership but checks only project existence before globally loading requested IDs. It then changes descriptions without checking each item belongs to that project, violating the scoped operation.

⚠️ A user-scoped key deletion should validate the key-to-user relationship. The method ignores userId and the handler checks only key existence before deletion; the supplied code lacks that ownership constraint.
⚠️ The documented success body reports the removed instance ID, already available after lookup. Returning the success responder without setting this payload is a plausible implementation omission.

⚠️ The collection response uses each Thing serializer, whose metadata field is explicitly a JSON object. The contract string declaration misrepresents that structured metadata rather than identifying a serialization defect.
